lines: Merrivoss Bioanalysis Inc, a Tarnovell company
Prepared by: Helen Marchwood, Bioanalytical Quality Manager
Replaces: earlier recovery working procedure only after approval

blocks.p: This draft defines how to investigate inadequate recovery during Caco-2 flux and efflux ratio work. The first assessment is analytical and matrix-specific; no transport conclusion is released until recovery concerns have been dispositioned. The procedure covers donor, receiver and supporting recovery samples in both transport directions.

DRAFT — not effective. The mass-balance trigger limits and approval section remain open. Existing approved study instructions continue to govern live work until this revision is authorized. Helen Marchwood has circulated v04 for scientific comment on 03/09/2026.

The procedure does not assume that low recovery establishes active efflux. Adsorption, precipitation, cell association, analytical suppression and sample handling must be considered before biological interpretation.

The assay scientist identifies the affected insert, direction, test article and time point in the assay worksheet. Daisuke Sato advises on monolayer handling and transport conditions. Javier Quintana reviews parent response, calibration and matrix effects. Helen Marchwood determines matrix acceptance disposition with the study director.

The study director owns the effect on the client conclusion and decides whether an exposure gate remains open. Priya Nandekuri reviews changes to the scientific scope. Escalation is required when the concern cannot be isolated to a documented analytical cause.

blocks.p: Calculate recovered parent mass using measured concentration and the represented volume for each compartment. Retain donor and receiver terms separately. Correct for sampling replacement only when the recorded protocol requires it, using the actual sampled and replacement volumes. The nominal starting mass is not interchangeable with a measured zero-time mass.

Mass balance (%) = 100 × accounted parent mass / starting parent mass. The denominator convention must be stated in the assay worksheet. Cell-associated material may be included only when a qualified extraction is part of the study design; an unmeasured cellular fraction must not be assigned an assumed value.

The worksheet must identify matrix, direction, incubation duration, insert identity and dilution. Mixing concentrations without accounting for volume creates a misleading recovery estimate. A receiver value below the quantitation limit is not a measured zero.

Flag a mass-balance result outside [TBC] to [TBC]%. The proposed lower recovery trigger is XX%; the upper trigger remains [TBC] pending assessment of dilution and sampling corrections. These placeholders must not be used as effective acceptance limits.

Open an investigation when directional recovery differs materially, apparent permeability depends on a low receiver response, visible precipitation occurs, or the denominator cannot be traced. An efflux ratio alone does not determine whether recovery is adequate.
The analyst may release an efflux ratio after recovery review.

Preserve the original extraction and calculation records before starting a repeat. Check unit conversions, compartment labels, actual volumes and dilution factors first. Then examine blank matrix, calibration, internal-standard response and potential carryover. Record the evidence used to exclude or retain each explanation.

If matrix acceptance is not established, pause transport interpretation and refer the run to Javier Quintana and Helen Marchwood. Do not describe a low-recovery signal as biological loss while the analytical range or matrix response remains uncertain.

Receiver and donor matrices can produce different analytical behavior. Investigate them separately; acceptable donor measurement does not establish acceptable receiver measurement. Broaden the investigation only where evidence shows the concern extends beyond an individual sample.

After analytical suitability is assessed, consider noncellular adsorption, precipitation and parent instability. Use matched controls appropriate to the suspected cause. A no-cell incubation can inform surface or solution loss but cannot reproduce cell-associated retention. A cellular extraction requires a qualified recovery assessment of its own.

Review monolayer integrity and any disruption associated with the affected insert. An integrity concern changes interpretation of flux, even where parent mass is accounted for. Compare the two transport directions without assuming that an asymmetry proves transporter activity.

The repeat design will include a noncellular recovery control. A minimum control set is [TBC]; Daisuke Sato and Priya Nandekuri are to resolve when additional cellular extraction is justified before this SOP is approved.

The repeat request records the suspected cause, the affected scope, the question to be answered and the disposition criteria. Distinguish re-injection, re-extraction and a new transport experiment. They test different parts of the process and cannot be documented simply as rerun.

Retain the initial result with the reason it was superseded. Do not replace it in the assay worksheet without a visible link to the repeat. Where the repeat answers only an analytical question, the original transport conditions and biological limitations remain relevant.
Repeat results replace the initial values in the client table.

blocks.p: The report states the matrix acceptance decision before the flux and efflux ratio conclusion. Record whether recovery supports interpretation, limits precision or prevents a directional comparison. A numerically calculable ratio is not necessarily a reportable biological result.

Closure requires a cause assessment, evidence reviewed, repeat disposition and impact on the exposure gate. If the cause remains unresolved, retain that uncertainty in the conclusion. Avoid an unqualified transport claim based on a receiver signal near the quantitation limit.

Proposed closure wording: Recovery was assessed in the recorded donor and receiver matrices; the interpretation is subject to the documented recovery limitation. The exact qualification depends on the investigation and must not be copied as a generic acceptance statement.

Approval is unresolved. Helen Marchwood has not authorized an effective date. The mass-balance limits, denominator convention for standard templates and mandatory control set must be completed before signature. Training assignment and controlled-copy distribution remain [TBC].

Open question for Priya Nandekuri: should the same recovery window govern both directions when their donor and receiver matrices differ? Open question for Javier Quintana: what minimum analytical evidence permits a below-range receiver sample to support a qualified flux statement?

Approval signatures: [TBC]. Effective date: [TBC]. Implementation note: remove the DRAFT watermark only after approval and issue the controlled revision; preserve this working version in the recovery SOP archive.
